solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sells call options hedging Shell?

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so the words hedging something enclose it inside their run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A trader on the stock market covers their position in Shell, the oil company, by selling call options.
explanation.walkthrough: The finance jargon is the disguise: hedging is a real trading term, and Shell looks like the oil company. SCALLOP sits across sellS CALL OPtions.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a kind of mollusc whose fan-shaped shell is familiar, and the word also names the shell itself.

clue.text: Dirac’s worked to incorporate minute phone component

indicators.note: something worked has been shaped or kneaded, so its letters have been moved about
to incorporate is to take into a body, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: the physicist's name with its possessive S, used as fodder
m is the standard abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Paul Dirac, the quantum physicist, labours to build a tiny part into a telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective meaning tiny, fitting a small phone part, but it is the noun, a unit of time. The physicist's name plus its possessive S is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A SIM card is the small chip inserted into a mobile handset that identifies the subscriber on the network.

clue.text: Nigella, having swapped nickel for gold, pirouetted briskly

indicators.note: a swap trades one thing out and another in, so letters are exchanged for new ones
a pirouette is a dancer's spin, so the letters are whirled round into a new order

blocks.note: the name as written, the starting word
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel, the letters taken out
or is gold in heraldry, the letters put in

explanation.surface: Nigella Lawson, the TV cook, trades her nickel for gold and spins quickly on one foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace NI in NIGELLA with OR to get ORGELLA, then rearrange. Or for gold is a heraldic term crosswords use constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the Italian musical tempo marking meaning at a lively, quick pace, so it serves as an adverb.

clue.text: Tag Jezebel’s last murder victim

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the queen's name
in Genesis Abel is killed by his brother Cain, the first murder

explanation.surface: A biblical crime report: the last man killed by the wicked queen Jezebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jezebel supplies only her last letter; the murder victim is Abel, killed by Cain, rather than anyone of Jezebel's.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag and a label are both small attached tickets giving a name, price or description of an item.

clue.text: Dad runs Susan over when crossing Sierra mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means read from bottom to top, backwards
a word crossing another straddles it, so it sits around it on both sides

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
r is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
the name as written, to be turned round
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Dad drives over Susan while going across the Sierra, a sorry mountain-road accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs Susan over' reads as a car accident, but runs is the cricket abbreviation and 'over' turns the name round, as a down clue reads from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Parnassus is a peak in central Greece, sacred in legend to Apollo and the Muses.

clue.text: Old principally Regency Somerset town where apples grow

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: o is the standard abbreviation for old
the first letter of the period name
Chard is a small market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A guidebook line about an old Regency-era town in Somerset, a county famed for its cider apples.
explanation.walkthrough: Chard is a small town in Somerset, in south-west England, where apple orchards and cider are famous, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a piece of land planted with fruit trees, so it is literally the place where apples grow.

clue.text: Hold forth over cost

blocks.note: o is the scorecard abbreviation for an over in cricket
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Someone ranting at length about the price of things.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, and O is its abbreviation on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a long, pompous speech, which is exactly what holding forth means.

clue.text: Area set aside for spokes people?

definitions.text: Area set aside for spokes people?

blocks.clueFragment: Area set aside for spokes people?
blocks.note: surface reading: a room reserved for spokespeople, official representatives who speak to the press
setter's reading: people who ride on spokes, that is on bicycle wheels, and the lane kept for them

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'spokespeople' into 'spokes people' and they become riders on spoked wheels. The answer also sounds like psychopath, an extra joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle path is a strip of ground reserved for bicycle riders, kept separate from cars and walkers.

clue.text: Prevented a vague, empty ending to Father Ted

indicators.note: an empty word has had its contents poured out, so just its outside letters stay
the ending of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the article as written
the first and final letters of the adjective
the final letter of the word
the name as written

explanation.surface: A review complaint that the sitcom Father Ted was spared a vague, hollow finale.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is an Irish TV sitcom about priests, but here 'Father' and 'Ted' part company: one gives only its last letter, the other goes in whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to prevent it or turn it aside before it happens, so averted means stopped in advance.

clue.text: Senior woman finished acquiring Asian currency

indicators.note: to acquire is to take something in and hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: done means completed
the yen is the money of Japan

explanation.surface: A retired woman, finished with work, takes up some foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished' reads as an adjective describing the woman, but it is a separate word that wraps around the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or longest-serving woman in some field, its female elder.

clue.text: Drinking establishment where I get the shakes?

definitions.text: Drinking establishment where I get the shakes?

blocks.clueFragment: Drinking establishment where I get the shakes?
blocks.note: surface reading: a pub where a heavy drinker ends up trembling
setter's reading: milkshakes, the drinks you order at this kind of place

explanation.walkthrough: 'The shakes' suggests alcoholic tremors, but the drinks are milkshakes, served at a cafe of the 1950s kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk bar is a snack bar or cafe that sells milky drinks, ice cream and light food rather than alcohol.

clue.text: Left in pain, mentally hollow, work to find the elixir of life

definitions.text: work to find the elixir of life

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside its boundaries
a hollow word has had its insides scooped out, so just its outer letters stay

blocks.note: an ache is a dull pain
l is the standard abbreviation for left
the first and final letters of the adverb

explanation.surface: A person left suffering and drained seeks a magic cure to live forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, and 'hollow' as empty-headed; they are an abbreviation and an instruction to keep only a word's outside. The long definition describes the medieval pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy was the medieval proto-science that sought to turn base metals into gold and brew a potion granting immortality.

clue.text: Full of cold, Frau Merkel drained Kaffee and sponge

indicators.note: something full of another holds it inside
a drained vessel has had its contents emptied out, so only its shell of outer letters stays

blocks.note: Angela Merkel was the German chancellor
c is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the first and final letters of the German word for coffee

explanation.surface: Angela Merkel, full of a cold, drinks up her coffee and has a slice of cake: a German Kaffee und Kuchen scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Merkel was Germany's chancellor from 2005 to 2021. The German coffee is fitting, and 'drained' sounds like finishing the cup, but it strips the word to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a very light, pale sponge cake made with whipped egg whites and no yolks.

clue.text: Each can eschew restaurants

blocks.note: ea is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price lists
a tin is a can of food

explanation.surface: Everyone is able to avoid eating out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb meaning is able to; it is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have your meal at home instead of going out, which is exactly avoiding dining establishments.

clue.text: That’s funny, doctor – LOL that’s funny!

definitions.note: an exclamation standing for an adjective; read as '(that's) funny'

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters are in a strange order

blocks.note: dr is the standard abbreviation for doctor
the internet abbreviation for laughing out loud, used as letters

explanation.surface: Someone texting a doctor about a joke, laughing out loud at how funny it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase appears twice with two jobs: first as the definition, then as the instruction to rearrange LOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry, odd or quirky way, the sense of funny in a wry comment.

clue.text: Minimal covering on to chill out

indicators.note: out here means disordered or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Advice to wear almost nothing when relaxing on a hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chill out' reads as a phrasal verb meaning relax, but 'out' is the instruction and 'chill' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single piece of fabric wrapped round the hips, about the least clothing a person can wear.

clue.text: After moving desk, go off and do a runner

indicators.note: moving things shifts them from their places, so the letters take new positions

blocks.note: the word as written, to be rearranged
eggs that go off become addled, or rotten

explanation.surface: An office worker, after their desk is relocated, storms off and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: To addle is to go rotten, as an egg does. To do a runner is British slang for running off, usually without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddle is informal for leaving in a hurry, and do a runner is British slang for fleeing quickly.

clue.text: Producer of duck egg blue bed cover?

blocks.note: the eider is a sea duck, so it lays duck eggs
feeling blue is feeling down, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A shopping description of a bedspread in the pale greenish colour called duck egg blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck egg blue is a real paint colour, so the phrase holds together; split it, and the bird that lays duck eggs is followed by a word for sad.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt originally stuffed with the soft breast feathers of eider ducks and laid over a bed.

clue.text: Badmouth schoolmarm? Journalist fired

blocks.note: to dis is slang for to insult or disparage
pupils address a female teacher as Miss
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter is sacked for trashing a stern schoolteacher in print.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dismissed means being sacked from a job, the same as being fired by an employer.

clue.text: Interpol finally to probe TV cook – hard, treacherous woman

indicators.note: finally means at the very end, so only the closing letter is kept
a probe is pushed into something, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Delia Smith is a famous British television cookery presenter
the final letter of the police organisation's name
h is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: International police investigate a celebrity chef, a hard and deceitful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is Britain's best-known TV cookery writer. The L goes inside DELIA, then H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Delilah betrays Samson to the Philistines by cutting his hair, so her name stands for a treacherous temptress.

clue.text: Betrayed only reservation, it’s said

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the clue works by the sound of the words

blocks.note: sole means only and a doubt is a reservation

explanation.surface: Someone felt let down, though they had just one doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' suggests a booking, and a sold-out show fits that reading, but here it means a misgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell out someone is to betray them, handing them over for personal gain, as in selling out your friends.

clue.text: Martha Stewart charged with reckless speeding

indicators.note: something charged with a substance is loaded with it, so the words are carrying the letters inside

blocks.note: the letters straddle the join between the first name and the surname

explanation.surface: A news report that Martha Stewart, the American lifestyle celebrity, has been charged with dangerous driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged with' is a legal phrase in the surface; in the wordplay it means loaded with. The answer sits across marTHA STEwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is excessive hurry, especially careless speed, as in the proverb more haste, less speed.

clue.text: Second husband began torrid affair

indicators.note: torrid means scorching or passionate, so the letters are heated up and thrown into disorder

blocks.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second
h is the abbreviation for husband in family trees
the word as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's second husband started a steamy romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' looks like the love affair of the surface, but it is the plain sense of a matter or business.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebang is informal for a thing, matter or business, chiefly in the phrase the whole shebang.

clue.text: Pay them to spread compassion

indicators.note: spreading is scattering about, so whatever is spread ends up in a new arrangement

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A charity appeal: give people money so that kindness gets around.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is at the front, so the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the ability to share and understand another person's feelings, closely akin to compassion or sympathy.

clue.text: Purplish ring returned when touring India

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel round it, so one piece goes all the way around another
something returned goes back the way it came, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A purple ring comes back from a trip round India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests jewellery, but it is the verb, a phone call. CALL goes around I, and the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale violet colour named after the flowering shrub, so it serves as an adjective meaning purplish.

clue.text: Gossip about great deal that’s very economical

blocks.note: dirt is scandalous gossip, as in dishing the dirt
c is short for circa, Latin for about
a heap is a large amount

explanation.surface: People chattering about a bargain that costs next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the link between gossip and its subject, but it gives C, from circa. 'Great deal' likewise reads as a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap is an idiom for costing extremely little, so something bought that way is very economical.

clue.text: Derek Trotter initially bags fine tableware

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
to bag something is to put it inside a sack, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: Del Boy, Derek Trotter, is the market trader in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses
the opening letter of the surname
f is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Del Boy, the wheeler-dealer of the sitcom Only Fools and Horses, snaps up some quality china.
explanation.walkthrough: Derek Trotter, known as Del Boy, is the market trader in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, so Derek is DEL. DEL plus T wraps around F.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of Delft, used for plates and dishes.

clue.text: Regularly cutting corners, son leaves

indicators.note: cutting at regular intervals removes every other letter, so only alternate ones are kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word
s is the family-tree abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A lazy son who keeps cutting corners walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as the verb, the son departing; it is the plural noun, salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a plant grown for its small peppery green leaves, eaten in salads and sandwiches.

clue.text: Paper available at one’s convenience?

blocks.note: surface reading: a newspaper you can pick up whenever it suits you
setter's reading: a public convenience is a British euphemism for a public toilet, and the paper is kept there

explanation.walkthrough: A public convenience is a British euphemism for a public toilet, and loo is British slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loo roll is a British term for a roll of toilet paper, the kind kept beside every lavatory.

clue.text: Ham – ace, cold open sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two slices, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: overt means done openly, not hidden
a is the playing-card abbreviation for ace
c is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A deli order: ham, top quality, served in a cold open sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all food, with 'ham' as meat and 'sandwiches' as a noun; ham is a verb for bad acting, and 'sandwiches' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way, which is exactly what overacting means.

clue.text: Iron Lady unveiled latest to get axe

indicators.note: a thing unveiled has its covering removed, so its outer letters come off
the latest item is the one that comes at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the Iron Lady was the nickname of Margaret Thatcher, UK prime minister; drop her surname's outer letters
the final letter of the verb

explanation.surface: A newspaper reveals that the Iron Lady's newest project is to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Lady is Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister in the 1980s. THATCHER stripped of its first and final letters leaves HATCHE, and the last of 'get' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small, short-handled axe used for chopping with one hand.

clue.text: Bouquet from Burgundy ages once swirled around

indicators.note: taking letters from a phrase means drawing them out of its interior
something swirled around has been spun to face the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: the letters from the tail of the first word through the start of the last

explanation.surface: A wine note: the aroma of a Burgundy that has aged, once swirled in the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests the aroma of wine, which the whole surface is about; here it means a bunch of flowers. The letters run backwards in burgundY AGES ONce.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of sweet-smelling flowers, a posy or small bouquet.
